function_v0.doc:
The agent asks the treasury to pay `amount` to `to` for `task_id`.
The contract enforces the policy and rejects any violation on-chain.
Only the free (unlocked) balance is spendable \xe2\x80\x94 funds reserved by open
escrows cannot be paid out directly.
function_v0.name: pay

fields.doc: Owner of the funds; the only one who can change the policy.
fields.name: admin

fields.doc: The root agent allowed to trigger payments when no session is active.
fields.name: agent

fields.doc: Max total spend allowed inside any rolling 24-hour window.
fields.name: daily_limit

fields.doc:
Max spend allowed in a SINGLE payment (a per-PAYMENT cap, checked per call).
`TaskSpent` accumulates spend per `task_id` for attribution only \xe2\x80\x94 it is NOT
capped against this limit, so several sub-cap payments to the same task_id are
allowed; the real cumulative bound is the rolling 24h `daily_limit`.
fields.name: per_task_limit

fields.doc: SEP-41 / SAC token the treasury holds and spends (e.g. USDC).
fields.name: token

udt_struct_v0.doc: An outcome-bound payment: `amount` is reserved (locked) in the treasury for\n`payee` against `task_id`, releasable on approval or refundable after `deadline`\n(UNIX seconds). The funds never leave until release \xe2\x80\x94 refund just unlocks them.
udt_struct_v0.name: Escrow

tuple_v0.doc: Spend bucketed per hour (`timestamp / 3600`) \xe2\x80\x94 the rolling 24h window sums\nthe last 24 buckets. Old buckets are simply never read again; persistent\nmin-TTL far exceeds 24h, so an in-window bucket can never be archived.
tuple_v0.name: HourSpent

void_v0.doc:
Poseidon Merkle root over the payee set a compliance proof is checked against.
Owner-declared (the whitelist itself is not enumerable on-chain), so the proof
asserts membership in *this* treasury's published payee set rather than one the
prover picked.
void_v0.name: WhitelistRoot

void_v0.doc: Most this treasury may hold after a `deposit`. Set once in the constructor, no setter.
void_v0.name: DepositCap

void_v0.doc: Most the agent may move in one UTC calendar month (0 / absent = no monthly limit).
void_v0.name: MonthlyLimit

tuple_v0.doc: Agent-moved value per month, keyed by `month_of(timestamp)`.
tuple_v0.name: MonthSpent

tuple_v0.doc: Most one payee may receive per UTC calendar month (absent = only the other limits).
tuple_v0.name: PayeeCap

void_v0.doc: The payees the current Leash may pay. Empty / absent = any approved payee.
void_v0.name: SessionPayees

udt_struct_v0.doc:
A time-bound, spend-capped agent credential. While a session is active
(`now < valid_until`) it is the ONLY spender \xe2\x80\x94 the root agent is replaced,
not complemented, so authorisation stays unambiguous and auditable. When it
expires or is revoked, spending falls back to `Config.agent`.
udt_struct_v0.name: Session

function_v0.doc: Total funds currently reserved by open escrows (treasury balance minus this\nis the spendable free balance).
function_v0.name: locked

function_v0.doc:
Fund the treasury from `from`, refusing anything that would take its balance above the
deposit cap. The cap is the beta's exposure bound while the code is unaudited.

A plain token transfer to the treasury's address does not pass through here \xe2\x80\x94 no
contract can refuse incoming SAC transfers \xe2\x80\x94 so the cap binds the app, the factory and
every client that funds through `deposit`, not a sender determined to go around it.
function_v0.name: deposit

function_v0.doc: Whitelist a payee. Admin-only.
function_v0.name: add_payee

function_v0.doc: Spend inside the rolling 24-hour window (the "daily" allowance).
function_v0.name: day_spent

function_v0.doc: The monthly cap on `payee`, or 0 when it has none.
function_v0.name: payee_cap

function_v0.doc: Rotate the root agent (the fallback spender when no session is active).\nAdmin-only \xe2\x80\x94 the recovery path if the root agent key is lost or leaked.
function_v0.name: set_agent

function_v0.doc: Update the spending limits, effective immediately. Admin-only. If the new\ndaily limit is below what the window already holds, spending resumes once\nthe window drains \xe2\x80\x94 that is the intended behaviour.
function_v0.name: set_limits

function_v0.doc: Freeze/unfreeze spending (pay, create_escrow, release_escrow). Admin-only.\nExit paths \xe2\x80\x94 refund_escrow, admin_withdraw, and every admin setter \xe2\x80\x94 keep\nworking while paused, so an incident can always be unwound.
function_v0.name: set_paused

function_v0.doc: Cumulative spend recorded against `task_id` \xe2\x80\x94 an attribution ledger, not a cap.\n(The per-call limit is `Config.per_task_limit`; the cumulative bound is the daily window.)
function_v0.name: task_spent

function_v0.doc: The current UTC calendar month as `year * 12 + (month - 1)` \xe2\x80\x94 the key every monthly\nfigure is stored under, so clients never re-derive the calendar themselves.
function_v0.name: this_month

function_v0.doc: Most this treasury takes in through `deposit` (0 = uncapped). Fixed at deploy.
function_v0.name: deposit_cap

function_v0.doc: The stored session, if any \xe2\x80\x94 including an expired one (callers compare\n`valid_until` to now; the contract itself ignores expired sessions).
function_v0.name: get_session

function_v0.doc: Agent-moved value in `month` (see `this_month`), escrow commitments included.
function_v0.name: month_spent

function_v0.doc: What `payee` has been paid (or had committed in escrow) in `month`.
function_v0.name: payee_spent

function_v0.doc: Delegate spending to a session agent. Admin-only. While the session is\nactive it is the only spender (see `Session`); setting a new session\noverwrites the old one and resets its spent counter (rotation).
function_v0.name: set_session

function_v0.doc:
Total agent-moved value inside the closed UTC day `period_id`
(`period_id = timestamp / 86400`) \xe2\x80\x94 the figure a compliance proof commits to.

Deliberately NOT `day_spent`: the rolling window answers "how much allowance is
left right now" and changes every hour, so a proof could never bind to it. This
sums the 24 fixed buckets of one calendar day, giving a value that is final once
the day closes and reads identically forever after.

"Moved" includes escrow commitments, not just settled payments \xe2\x80\x94 `create_escrow`
charges the same buckets, because locking the balance is the agent exercising its
budget whether or not the funds ever leave.

24 persistent reads, one fewer than `rolling_spent` already performs per spend.
function_v0.name: period_spent

function_v0.doc: Remove a payee from the whitelist. Admin-only.
function_v0.name: remove_payee

function_v0.doc:
Atomic init at deploy time (no front-runnable `initialize`).
Limits are validated here so a treasury can never exist with a policy
that contradicts itself (e.g. per-task above daily).

`deposit_cap` (0 = none) is fixed for the treasury's life: nothing can raise it, so a
factory that pins one hands out treasuries the owner cannot over-fund through `deposit`.
function_v0.name: __constructor

function_v0.doc:
Agent reserves `amount` for `payee` against a future-delivered task. The funds
stay in the treasury (locked, not transferred) until released on approval or
refunded after `deadline`. Subject to the same payee gate + per-task limit +
session cap as a direct payment; the rolling window is charged here, at
commitment time (see the reasoning inline below).
function_v0.name: create_escrow

function_v0.doc:
After the deadline, the agent reclaims an undelivered escrow \xe2\x80\x94 the lock is
released back to the treasury's free balance. No transfer, no spend recorded,
and the session budget is NOT restored (conservative: the cap bounds what a
session may commit). Deliberately works while paused (exit path).
function_v0.name: refund_escrow

function_v0.doc:
Most `payee` may receive per UTC calendar month. Admin-only; 0 removes the cap. The cap
does not approve the payee \xe2\x80\x94 it narrows what an approved (or reputation-gated) payee
can be paid. Capping the agent's own float address is what bounds money that has left
the treasury's protection.
function_v0.name: set_payee_cap

function_v0.doc:
Owner reclaims free (unlocked) funds with their own signature. Deliberately
exempt from pause, the payee gate, and the rolling window: those bound
*delegated* agent spending, and the exit path must work exactly when limits
are exhausted or spending is frozen. Escrow-locked funds stay locked (the
commitment to payees survives; refund is the escape hatch for those).
function_v0.name: admin_withdraw

function_v0.doc:
Admin (the owner / hirer) approves delivery \xe2\x86\x92 release the locked funds to the
payee. The rolling window was already charged when the escrow was created, so
release does not check or charge it again; the spend is accounted per task
exactly like a direct `pay`.
function_v0.name: release_escrow

function_v0.doc: Instantly revoke the session \xe2\x80\x94 spending falls back to the root agent.\nAdmin-only; deliberately works while paused (incident response).
function_v0.name: revoke_session

function_v0.doc: The payees the current Leash is restricted to; empty when it may pay any approved one.
function_v0.name: session_payees

function_v0.doc: The payee-set Merkle root this treasury publishes, or `None` if the owner never\ndeclared one (in which case no compliance proof can be checked against it).
function_v0.name: whitelist_root

function_v0.doc:
A Leash for one task: like `set_session`, but the agent may only pay the payees
listed here (each must still pass the whitelist / reputation gate). This is what the
owner signs when approving an agent's budget request \xe2\x80\x94 once, for the whole task.
Admin-only.
function_v0.name: set_task_budget

function_v0.doc: Most the agent may move per UTC calendar month, across every payee. Admin-only;\n0 removes the monthly limit. Like the daily limit, lowering it below what the month\nalready holds simply stops spending until the month turns.
function_v0.name: set_monthly_limit

function_v0.doc:
Publish the Merkle root of the payee set that compliance proofs are checked
against. Admin-only: the root IS the owner's policy statement, so an agent that
could write it would be choosing the payee set its own proof is verified against.

The root is not derived from `DataKey::Payee` \xe2\x80\x94 the whitelist is a key-per-payee
map with no on-chain enumeration, and the circuit's Poseidon hash has no host
implementation to rebuild it with. The owner computes it off-chain and anchors it
here; the event makes every change auditable.
function_v0.name: set_whitelist_root

function_v0.doc:
Admin unilaterally cancels an open escrow \xe2\x80\x94 the lock returns to the free
balance, nothing is paid, no deadline needed. This is the incident-response
path: a compromised agent could otherwise tie up the whole treasury in
escrows it alone can refund. Deliberately works while paused (exit path);
the session budget is NOT restored (consistent with refund).
function_v0.name: admin_cancel_escrow

function_v0.doc: The active reputation gate, if any: `(registry, min_reputation)`.
function_v0.name: get_reputation_policy

function_v0.doc:
Set (or update) the reputation gate. Admin-only. With `min_reputation > 0`,
a payee that is NOT on the whitelist can still be paid when its score from
`registry` is >= `min_reputation` \xe2\x80\x94 turning the static allowlist into an
earned-trust gate. Set `min_reputation = 0` to disable (whitelist-only).
function_v0.name: set_reputation_policy
